column1: 50305642	"Hi HN! Today I wanna show you a thing that solved my headache (and maybe will solve yours too). The only reason I created this tool is a mess around my SSH keys and configs. I am constantly working with a bunch of devices via SSH (such as Raspberry Pi's
column4: etc.) and I never knew whether permissions were right and there was no way to tell a strong key from a weak one. So
column5:
meet Keyward

Main features:

1. Lists every key with algorithm
column9:
date of last modification and whether it has a passphrase

2. Runs a security audit for all of your keys
column10:
config and permissions in ~/.ssh and grades the result with A-F score. Also here you can find fix suggestions for every problem

3. Editor for ~/.ssh/config with byte-identical round-trip so all your comments are untouched

4. Convenient key generator for those who have difficulties using the ""ssh-keygen"" command

5. Backup of your keys
column11:
config and encrypted metadata so u can move all of your files quickly and safely and restore them on another machine

6. Headless CLI
column12:
e.g. keyward audit --json --fail-on=warning

7. Look through your known_hosts file to see address
column13:
key type and fingerprint and delete unnecessary records

Private keys are deliberately NOT encrypted by Keyward
column14:
they stay protected by their own passphrases.

No daemon
column16: no config to learn before starting
column17: just a single static Go binary. The security-sensitive core's direct dependencies are only filippo.io/age and golang.org/x/crypto
column18:
releases are cosign-signed. Threat model is in SECURITY.md

Install:

   brew install gateway-of-last-resort/tap/keyward for macOS/Linux
